questions.q: Why did this course deliberately avoid repeating the same combination of architecture domains across its seven case studies?
options: Because Salesforce certification rules forbid reusing domain combinations
Because each domain can legally only be taught once per course
Because the goal was practicing the same underlying judgment across enough different shapes of problem that the judgment itself transfers, rather than memorizing one playbook
Because repeating domains would have required more screenshots
questions.explain: No two scenarios leaned on the same domain combination on purpose — the point was transferable judgment, not a memorized single playbook.

questions.q: Within Chapter 2's methodology chain, why can't risk prioritization (Lesson 11) happen sensibly before stating assumptions (Lesson 10)?
options: Because you can't prioritize risk sensibly without first knowing which assumptions you're actually making about the scenario
Because risk prioritization and assumptions are actually unrelated skills
Because Lesson 11 must always come before Lesson 10 in the outline regardless of content
Because risk prioritization requires a completed blueprint first
questions.explain: The chain's dependency runs requirements to assumptions to risk to blueprint to rejected alternatives — each step needs the output of the one before it, which is why assumptions have to come before risk prioritization.

questions.q: Which case study combined Omni-Channel routing, event-driven outage alerts, and tiered storage for scale?
options: Alder Trust Bank (financial services onboarding)
Fenwick State University (higher education advising)
Carrow Equipment (manufacturing dealer network)
Nimbus Mobile (telecom omnichannel service)
questions.explain: Nimbus Mobile's telecom scenario from Lesson 6 specifically combined skills-based Omni-Channel routing, an event-driven outage-alert pattern, and a tiered large-data-volume storage strategy for scale.

questions.q: What does the "Communication" rubric self-check question in this wrap-up lesson actually ask you to evaluate?
options: Whether you used a microphone during your presentation
Whether your most recent walkthrough read as one connected story across domains, or still as separate topics bolted together
Whether your diagrams were drawn in color
Whether you answered every question with exactly one sentence
questions.explain: This directly reuses the Communication category's actual concern from Lesson 20 — narrative connectedness across the domain walkthrough, not surface-level delivery mechanics.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what should happen to the portfolio built in Lesson 19 once this course ends?
options: It should be carried forward and reused, since it was built specifically to support future interviews, review boards, and ongoing reference, not to be retired
It should be deleted, since the course is now complete
It should be submitted to Salesforce for official certification credit
It should be rewritten from scratch for every new course in the path
questions.explain: The wrap-up explicitly says the portfolio is built to be reused, not retired the moment this course ends — its value continues into real interviews and engagements.
